eventMetadata.context_description: The fragmented 2028 Democratic field remains wide open more than two years before primaries, with no formal candidacies declared after the party's 2024 loss. Trader pricing reflects this uncertainty, as Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez draws support from progressive and younger voters while Gavin Newsom and Jon Ossoff compete on name recognition and perceived electability among moderates. Recent DNC decisions on early primary states, including South Carolina first, have begun shaping strategy, though polling and power rankings show splits along ideological lines. Developments such as candidate announcements, Senate or gubernatorial races, endorsements from party factions, or shifts in national polling could consolidate support and widen gaps among the current leaders.

title: Fed Decision in September?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's September 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for September 15-16, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their September meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent softer U.S. economic data has strengthened trader consensus around no change at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting. July employment figures showed negative payroll growth and a dip in labor force participation, while retail sales contracted and July inflation readings came in line with or below expectations. These outcomes have tempered earlier concerns over sticky price pressures that prompted three hawkish dissents and a 9-3 hold vote at the July meeting. FOMC minutes highlighted broad-based inflation risks and support among several participants for earlier tightening, yet incoming data has lowered the implied probability of a 25 basis point hike. The next round of inflation and jobs reports before mid-September will remain the key variables shaping final positioning.
